title: What leadership is
blurb: Define leadership in APM terms and tell it apart from management, the classic exam pairing.
question: A project manager has a baselined plan, a tight budget and a team that does exactly what it is told, but no one seems committed to the goal. Which part of the project manager's role is missing, and what does it involve?

teach.body: Formally, leadership is the ability to establish vision and direction, to influence and align others towards a common purpose, and to empower and inspire people to achieve success. In plain English: a leader shows people where the project is going and why it matters, gets everyone pulling the same way, and then gives them the confidence and freedom to deliver. It is about people and purpose, not paperwork.

teach.caption: Learn the three parts of the definition in this order: they are what exam options are built from.

teach.h: Leadership is not the same as management
teach.body: Management plans, organises and controls: it builds the schedule, sets the budget, allocates resources and monitors progress against the baseline. Leadership sets direction, influences and inspires: it explains the purpose, builds commitment and helps people through change and setbacks. A project needs both. Management without leadership gives a tidy plan nobody believes in; leadership without management gives enthusiasm with no control. Good project managers do both.

teach.h: Leadership vs management at a glance
Two skill sets, one project manager
teach.caption: Some activities sit in both: communicating and deciding are tools of a leader and a manager alike.

teach.body: Amira is moving a GP surgery to a new building. As a manager she builds the schedule, agrees the budget and books the removal firm. As a leader she explains to anxious staff why the move will improve patient care, involves them in planning the new layout, and rallies the team when the IT installation slips. The plan tells people what to do; her leadership makes them want to do it.

rows.label: Trusting people to choose how to work

teach.note: Ask: is this about controlling the work, or about people's direction and commitment?

teach.text: Exam distractors describe MANAGEMENT tasks as if they were leadership: monitoring the budget, updating the schedule, recording risks, enforcing procedures. Leadership is about vision, influence and inspiration. Also, leadership does not depend on job title or formal authority: it works through influence.

items: Leadership: establish vision and direction, influence and align others to a common purpose, empower and inspire people to succeed.
Management: plan, organise and control the work.
A project needs both; good project managers do both.
Leadership works through influence, not just position or authority.

summary: You can now define leadership as establishing vision and direction, influencing and aligning others to a common purpose, and empowering and inspiring people to succeed. You can also separate it from management, which plans, organises and controls, and explain why a project manager needs both.

A.q: Complete the statement: leadership is the ability to establish vision and direction, to influence and align others towards a common purpose, and to…
options: plan, organise and control the work to budget
empower and inspire people to achieve success
monitor progress against the agreed baseline
allocate resources fairly to every package
A.why: The third part of the definition is to empower and inspire people to achieve success.

whyNot.0: Planning, organising and controlling describes management, not leadership.
whyNot.2: Monitoring against a baseline is a management control activity.
whyNot.3: Allocating resources is a planning and management task.

A.q: Which activity is mainly an example of leadership rather than management?
options: Updating the schedule after a change
Producing the monthly cost report
Checking work against the quality plan
Rallying the team behind a shared goal
A.why: Rallying people behind a shared goal is influencing, aligning and inspiring: the heart of leadership.

whyNot.0: Updating the schedule is planning and control, a management task.
whyNot.1: Cost reporting is monitoring and control, a management task.
whyNot.2: Checking work against a plan is quality control, part of managing.

A.q: Which statement best describes how leadership and management relate on a project?
options: An effective PM needs to use both of them
Leadership removes the need for management
Management only applies on large projects
Leadership belongs to the sponsor alone
A.why: Management plans, organises and controls; leadership sets direction and inspires. Good project managers do both.

whyNot.1: Without management there is no plan or control, however inspiring the leader.
whyNot.2: Every project, whatever its size, needs planning and control.
whyNot.3: Leadership is needed throughout the project, not only from the sponsor; the PM leads the team.

B.q: A project manager tells her team why the new system matters to patients and describes what success will look like. Which element of leadership is she mainly showing?
options: Controlling the agreed work packages
Organising the resource plan
Establishing vision and direction
Monitoring progress to plan
B.why: Explaining the purpose and the picture of success is establishing vision and direction.

whyNot.0: Controlling work packages is a management activity, not about purpose.
whyNot.1: Organising resources is planning and management.
whyNot.3: Monitoring progress is control; she is describing the destination, not tracking against it.

B.q: Which TWO of the following are features of leadership? 1. Inspiring people  2. Producing the budget  3. Aligning others to a common purpose  4. Baselining the schedule
options: 1 and 3
1 and 2
2 and 4
3 and 4
B.why: Inspiring people (1) and aligning others to a common purpose (3) are both in the definition of leadership.

whyNot.1: Producing the budget (2) is a management task.
whyNot.2: Both the budget (2) and the schedule baseline (4) are management tasks.
whyNot.3: Baselining the schedule (4) is planning and control, not leadership.

B.q: Which of the following is NOT part of leadership?
options: Influencing others
Empowering people
Inspiring the team
Controlling costs
B.why: Controlling costs is a management control activity. The other three are all in the definition of leadership.

whyNot.0: Influencing and aligning others is part of the definition of leadership.
whyNot.1: Empowering people is part of the definition of leadership.
whyNot.2: Inspiring people to succeed is part of the definition of leadership.

C.q: Halfway through an office relocation a key supplier fails and the team is demoralised. The schedule has already been re-planned. What should the project manager do next as a leader?
options: Re-baseline the cost plan once again
Restate the goal and rebuild morale
Escalate the issue to the PMO at once
Add the failure to the risk register
C.why: The re-planning (management) is done; the leadership need now is to restate direction and inspire a demoralised team.

whyNot.0: Re-baselining costs is management control and does nothing for morale.
whyNot.2: Escalation may be needed for the supplier, but it does not lead the team through the setback.
whyNot.3: The supplier failure has happened, so it is an issue, not a risk; and recording it does not lead people.

C.q: A project manager has excellent plans and controls, but the team feels no ownership and engagement is low. What is most likely missing?
options: A more detailed schedule
Tighter change control
Effective leadership
A formal quality plan
C.why: Plans and controls are in place (management). Low ownership and engagement point to missing leadership: direction, influence and inspiration.

whyNot.0: More schedule detail adds control, not commitment.
whyNot.1: Change control manages scope; it does not build engagement.
whyNot.3: A quality plan defines standards; it will not create ownership.

C.q: Which statement about leadership on a project is correct?
options: It works through influence, not just authority
It mainly depends on holding a senior title
It is mainly about controlling the budget
It is only really needed once a team is failing
C.why: Leadership influences and aligns people towards a common purpose; it does not rely only on formal authority or position.

whyNot.1: Anyone who sets direction and influences others can lead; a title is not required.
whyNot.2: Controlling the budget is management, not leadership.
whyNot.3: Leadership is needed from the start to set direction, not only when things go wrong.

reteach.title: Think of a music festival
reteach.question: A festival needs someone with a spreadsheet and someone who makes the crew want to work through the night. Which is leadership and which is management?

blocks.body: The festival organiser books the bands, fixes the budget, orders the toilets and sets the stage times: that is management. But when a storm hits on Saturday, someone has to gather the crew, remind them why thousands of fans came, decide together how to keep the show going and give each team the freedom to fix its own area: that is leadership. A great festival director does both.

rows.label: Before the gates open
values: Shares the vision of the event

blocks.text: If an option is about plans, budgets, schedules, registers or reports, it is management. If it is about vision, influence, alignment, empowerment or inspiration, it is leadership.

explain.body: A leader paints a clear picture of where the project is going and why it matters. Direction gives every decision a reference point: does this move us towards the goal or away from it?

test.q: What does establishing direction mainly give a project team?
options: A detailed breakdown of the costs
A list of every known project risk
A signed-off business case
A clear sense of where it is going
test.why: Direction tells the team where the project is heading and why, so effort points the same way.

whyNot.0: A cost breakdown is a management planning output.
whyNot.1: A risk list comes from risk management, not from setting direction.
whyNot.2: The business case is owned by the sponsor; signing it off is governance, not leadership.

explain.body: Project managers often lead people they do not line-manage, so they rely on influence: listening, explaining, persuading and building relationships. Aligning means getting everyone working towards the same common purpose rather than their own separate goals.

test.q: Leadership involves aligning others. What does this mean?
options: Placing people in a strict reporting line
Getting people pulling towards one goal
Giving every member identical tasks
Matching tasks to the cheapest people
test.why: Aligning means bringing people together behind a common purpose so their efforts point the same way.

whyNot.0: A reporting line is organisational structure, not alignment of purpose.
whyNot.2: Identical tasks ignore people's skills and say nothing about shared purpose.
whyNot.3: Matching tasks to cost is resource planning, a management activity.

explain.body: Empowering means trusting people with decisions and the freedom to choose how they work. Inspiring means giving them energy and belief, especially when things get hard. Together they turn compliance into commitment.

steps.label: Ownership
steps.sub: People feel the work is theirs

test.q: Which behaviour best shows a leader empowering the team?
options: Approving every decision personally
Writing all work instructions alone
Letting members decide how to work
Keeping key information to the board
test.why: Empowerment means trusting people with decisions, such as how to carry out their own work.

whyNot.0: Approving every decision personally is micromanagement, the opposite of empowerment.
whyNot.1: Writing all the instructions alone takes ownership away from the team.
whyNot.3: Withholding information stops people making good decisions themselves.

explain.body: Management plans, organises and controls the work. Leadership sets direction, influences and inspires the people doing it. They are different, complementary skill sets, and a good project manager uses both.

test.q: Which activity is mainly management rather than leadership?
options: Organising resources to the plan
Inspiring the team after a setback
Sharing a vision of the end result
Building commitment to the goal
test.why: Organising resources to the plan is a management task: plan, organise, control.

whyNot.2: Sharing a vision is establishing direction, a leadership task.
whyNot.3: Building commitment is influencing and aligning, a leadership task.
